paper_metadata.title: Data is often loadable in short depth: Quantum circuits from tensor networks for finance, images, fluids, and proteins

summary: The paper introduces AMLET, a tensor-network-based compiler for amplitude encoding that loads length-M classical vectors into log2(M) qubits with depth/accuracy tradeoffs. It reports that 16-qubit instances can be prepared in fewer than 90 layers, with AMLET reducing depth by about 8% to 25% versus a layer-by-layer loader, while exact general amplitude encoding would require depths on the order of 2^15 to 2^15+ for the cited 12- and 16-qubit cases.

experiments.description: Tensor-network-based quantum circuit compilation for amplitude encoding of real-world classical data, evaluated on finance, images, turbulent fluid velocity, and protein atomic position datasets using the AMLET algorithm and compared against a layer-by-layer tensor-network loader.

algorithm.variant: AMLET (Automatic Multi-layer Loader Exploiting TNs) for amplitude encoding state preparation

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Load a length-M classical vector into log2(M) qubits; circuits are compiled from tensor networks with depth/accuracy tradeoff.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Approximate state preparation / data loading: prepare a quantum state whose amplitudes approximate the normalized classical data vector under application-specific error thresholds.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: No optimization; truncation/splitting in tensor-network compilation; ancilla-free construction.

problem_instance.description: Four data-loading benchmarks: finance time series, images, turbulent fluid velocity, and protein atomic coordinates.
problem_instance.dataset_name: Intel Image Classification; curated turbulence dataset; huge stock price data intraday minute bar; Protein Data Bank entries 1VVJ, 3I30, 3JA1

dataset_specification.description: Images from Intel Image Classification dataset; fluid data from a curated turbulent velocity dataset; finance from minute-by-minute S&P 500, NIKKEI 225, DAX 30, EUROSTOXX; proteins from PDB structures 1VVJ, 3I30, 3JA1.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Images encoded in row-major format with RGB grouped by color; fluid data encodes only the velocity component along bulk flow and enforces bounded error and momentum conservation; finance uses minute-by-minute intraday data with trading-hour discontinuities; proteins use non-overlapping sequences of atoms and RMSD-based comparison.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Numerical experiments across multiple qubit counts and depths; compare AMLET vs layer-by-layer loader; evaluate application-specific error thresholds and report depth ranges and reductions.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Tensor-network decomposition, SVD truncation, tensor expansion/splitting, reindexing; data normalization and application-specific thresholding.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compare approximate loaded state to target vector using application-specific error metrics; report depth and fidelity/error trends.

speedup_claims.factor: exponential depth reduction relative to exact general amplitude encoding
speedup_claims.conditions: for exact state preparation of a length-M vector into n qubits without ancillas
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states exact loading generally requires exponential depth; AMLET provides shorter-depth approximate loading, not a proven asymptotic speedup.

speedup_claims.conditions: at 16 qubits across the reported datasets
speedup_claims.caveats: Reduction is reported for the 16-qubit case; exact per-dataset values are not fully enumerated in text.

speedup_claims.factor: D < 200 for the largest known protein
speedup_claims.conditions: if the observed protein-depth trend persists
speedup_claims.caveats: This is an extrapolation from observed scaling, not a measured result.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Circuit construction depth is depth-tunable; for bounded constant depth, classical construction scales at most O(M).
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(M) for bounded depth using naive matrix routines; general exact amplitude encoding requires exponential depth in n without ancillas.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: No hardware execution; only numerical circuit compilation and depth analysis for amplitude encoding.
limiting_factors: No demonstrated speedup over classical baselines
Primary contribution is reduced circuit depth for data loading
Classical data loading remains a bottleneck

notes: No physical QPU is used; this is a circuit-compilation/numerical study, so hardware.type inferred as simulator_other/not specified.

The paper discusses loading into log2(M) qubits but does not give a single fixed qubit count for the experiment; qubit counts vary by dataset and are partially mentioned (e.g., 14 qubits for images, up to 16 qubits in summary), so num_qubits is not a single explicit value.
Depth statements such as D < 90 and per-dataset depth trends are explicitly reported.
The paper does not claim an asymptotic quantum speedup over classical loading; it emphasizes reduced depth for practical data loading.
The paper presents AMLET as a tensor-network compilation method for amplitude encoding, not as an end-to-end quantum advantage demonstration.
It reports shorter depths than a layer-by-layer loader and much shorter depths than exact amplitude encoding, but does not show practical quantum advantage on a real device.
